page.layout: One page of text. At the top, a woodcut ornamental border. Below it, a centred title in capitals and a centred heading. Then one column of running text with a large woodcut initial D at its left. At the foot, a signature and a catchword at the right.

main_text.head: DISSERTATIO PHILOLOGICO-ISAGOGICA AD CHRONOLOGIAM S. ET ECCLES. PRIMA.
De TEMPORE IN GENERE, DIE ET SEPTIMANA.
main_text.p: DOctrinam temporis, saltem isagogicam, cum Philologia S. conjunctissimam, non immeritò ad θεοπνευ-στίαν & apparatum Studii Theologici requirunt, qui tyronibus de recta ejus feliciter instituendi ratione praecipiunt. Necessitatem etiam fatebuntur haud inviti, quotquot olim futuri Sacrarum Literatum interpretes non in facilimis tantùm & obviis consistere volunt, sed, qua sunt erectiori indole praediti, ad amplioris cognitionis profectum in Scripturis & Historia cùm sacra, tùm Ecclesiastica, quatenus possunt debentque, contendunt. Qua etiam de causa iis, qui privatâ nostrâ qualicunque opellâ in Philologia Hebr. hactenus utuntur, exercendis hanc & secuturas aliquot, si Deus dederit, dissertatiunculas destinamus. Interea verò,

page.notes: The initial D is a large woodcut letter, joined to the first word as "Doctrinam". The Greek word in the text is set across a line end and is only partly legible in the scan; the reading θεοπνευστίαν is my best reconstruction. The heading "De" is in a decorative script and is set as a separate line. The signature "A 2" appears at the foot left; the catchword "ut" at the foot right.
